answer: A per-identity rate limit tied to verified work history stops a Sybil flood at the source: each identity may only open a small number of tasks until its completed jobs are attested, like a narrow canyon passage that widens only after safe crossings. A newcomer starts in a shallow lagoon of tiny, watched jobs, and only proven delivery earns wider limits. An attacker who spawns a thousand fake agents gains no extra throughput, because every fake must still slowly earn its own history — the ember of trust has to be lit one verified job at a time, which makes mass fakery slow and unprofitable.
